statement: For $i = \sqrt{-1}$, what is the value of $(1 + i)^{6}$?

choices.misconception: I raised each term to the sixth power separately, so I got $1^{6} + i^{6} = 1 - 1 = 0$.
I squared $1 + i$ term by term and used $i^{2} = 1$, getting 2, so I said $(1 + i)^{6} = 2^{3} = 8$.
I found $(1 + i)^{2} = 2i$ and $(2i)^{3} = 8i^{3}$, but then I used $i^{3} = i$ instead of $i^{3} = -i$.

hints: Expanding six factors is slow. Start with $(1 + i)^{2}$.

solutions.elegant: In polar form, $1 + i$ has length $\sqrt{2}$ and angle $45^\circ$. Its sixth power has length $(\sqrt{2})^{6} = 8$ and angle $6 \cdot 45^\circ = 270^\circ$, which points straight down: $-8i$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
